title: Marketplace FastPass: Listing Slate & QA Notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
Quick staging doc to capture the smallest, highest-impact asset set and QA checks so we can fast-track 3 partner listings in the next 6 weeks. This is intentionally prescriptive — we want a reproducible FastPass checklist that product marketing + partner ops can run without repeatedly re-negotiating copy or asset specs.

Audience:
- PM/Partner rep packaging the listing
- Creative / Content lead prepping screenshots and short video
- Engineering contact for technical onboarding (integration + metering)
- GTM ops for SKU mapping and trial config

TL;DR (for exec skim):
- Goal: Publish 3 curated marketplace listings (AWS, Azure, GCP) with matching copy variants and validated metering by M+6 weeks.
- Scope: Minimal assets (hero screenshot, 30s demo video, 1-line elevator + 3 variants of body copy), pricing SKU mapping, and integration smoke tests.
- Success metrics: listing live + first trial created within 14 days of publish; listing view -> trial CVR >= 4% in first 30 days.

Priority buckets (how to triage assets/effort):
1) Must-have (FastPass): 1-line, 50-word, 150-word descriptions; 1 hero screenshot (1280x720), short list of capabilities (3 bullets), billing SKU id, basic support contact, privacy and data residency callout.
2) High: 30s annotated demo video (mp4), 3 additional screenshots (console flows), one customer quote (if available), 1 short FAQ.
3) Nice-to-have: localized copy (EN/FR/DE), technical architecture diagram, benchmark snippet (latency/cost), deeper pricing tiers.

Copy variants (first drafts — pick one per listing):
- Elevator (one line): "Run production-grade LLM inference with predictable latency and unified tooling across hosted, dedicated and private deployments."
- 50-word blurb: "Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that helps teams ship LLM features reliably and affordably. Choose hosted, reserved (Dedicated), or private deployments while monitoring cost and latency with per-route dashboards and rollout controls."
- 150-word description (no marketing fluff, for technical buyers): "Redwood Inference delivers a unified runtime and control-plane for serving large language models at production scale. Our GPU-optimized serving engine supports continuous batching, KV cache management, and quantization-friendly execution across public cloud and private deployments. Teams get predictable latency SLAs, route-level observability, and automated fallbacks to keep apps online. Out-of-the-box integrations include model cataloging, rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback), and cost optimization suggestions. Ideal for product teams building chat, generation, and embedding workloads that must balance latency, cost, and compliance."

Feature bullets (short):
- Single API for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking
- Streaming responses + function/tool calling
- Dedicated GPU pools with predictable throughput
- VPC/private deploy options + KMS integration
- Console with token-level cost and latency breakdowns

Tone guide (for vendor marketplace constraints):
- Prioritize clarity and concrete capabilities over superlatives.
- Avoid proprietary model claims (we list model variants but not claimed superiority).
- Include security/compliance sums in plain language (e.g., "supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs").

Technical preflight checklist (FastPass minimal):
- Billing/Metering
  - Confirm SKU ID and one-line pricing descriptor (per-token / per-embedding basis).
  - Smoke test: create trial customer and confirm first metered event shows up in marketplace billing logs. (JIRA-3452 captures steps)
- Authentication
  - Confirm OAuth/service principal flow works from marketplace landing (app registration + redirect).
  - Validate token exchange sample script is included in listing notes.
- Integration artifacts
  - Provide sandbox API key / test-mode endpoint for marketplace validation team.
  - Provide sample curl + SDK snippet (Node + Python) — copy trimmed to <= 5 lines for listing panel.
- Assets
  - Hero screenshot (1280x720, PNG/JPG) — highlight Console route dashboard and cost breakdown.
  - 3x supporting screenshots (800px min width) — annotate with short captions.
  - Optional: 30s MP4 demo (720p) — include caption track file if possible.
- Security & Compliance notes
  - Short security statement (1-2 lines) and link to SOC2 page/whitepaper.
  - Data residency options: list cloud regions and outline Private deployment option.
- Documentation links
  - Quickstart guide URL (must be stable): https://docs.redwood.ai/marketplace-quickstart
  - Integration checklist (confluence link in linked_artifacts)

QA matrix (what marketplace validation will check + owner):
- Field mapping: Title, Short description, Long description, Tags, Categories — verify no truncation and acceptable length. Owner: Maya.
- Copy accuracy: no unsupported claims (legal check). Owner: Legal (Diego to ping).
- Asset rendering: screenshots scale correctly in AWS/azure UIs. Owner: Creative (Liam).
- Billing events: first metered usage appears in both Redwood usage logs and marketplace billing sandbox. Owner: Engineering (Eng-oncall).
- Trial provisioning: trial button triggers onboarding flow and creates a sandbox account. Owner: Partner Ops.

Risk register (quick):
- Risk: mismatch between SKU and backend metering key -> mitigation: tabletop with marketplace rep and run metering smoke test. Owner: Asha.
- Risk: hero screenshot reveals internal URLs -> mitigation: scrub and use staging data. Owner: Liam.
- Risk: listing copy flagged by marketplace compliance -> mitigation: pre-send to marketplace PM + legal review before publish. Owner: Diego.

Rollout plan (6-week cadence):
- Week 0: Freeze FastPass copy + hero screenshot and choose SKU mapping.
- Week 1: Engineering smoke tests (billing + trial).
- Week 2: Submit listing to marketplace validation (AWS/Azure/GCP).
- Week 3: Address validation feedback.
- Week 4: Prepare go-live comms + docs.
- Week 5: Publish and monitor initial telemetry.
- Week 6: First-read trial -> SQL handoff for qualified leads.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Asha: finalize SKU mapping and pricing line (ETA: 2026-03-17).
- Liam: produce hero screenshot + 3 captions, upload to shared assets (ETA: 2026-03-12).
- Maya: prepare 5-line Node + Python snippet and quickstart link (ETA: 2026-03-14).
- Diego: legal quick-check on claims + security blurb (ETA: 2026-03-15).
- Eng-oncall: run billing smoke test and post results to JIRA-3452 (ETA: 2026-03-18).

Notes to self / open questions (explicitly flagged):
- Q1: Do marketplaces require separate region-specific listings for Private deployments? (Ping product-privacy)
- Q2: Is the 30s video allowed autoplay? (marketplace policy varies by vendor)
- Q3: Can we include a short benchmark table in the listing? If yes, need allowed format.

Slack & comms refs (for quick traceability):
- #marketplace-launch thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C12345678/p1612345678000100
- PM sticky: @maya (we'll sync Mon 10am PT)

Appendix: Example short copy variants to swap into panels (pick one):
- Variant A (developer-forward): "Developer-first inference platform: predictable latency, per-route cost visibility, and unified runtime for hosted/dedicated/private deployments."
- Variant B (enterprise-forward): "Production-grade LLM inference with SLA-backed dedicated capacity and private deployment options for regulated workloads."
- Variant C (outcome-forward): "Ship LLM features faster: consistent performance, lower token costs, and built-in fallbacks to keep your app online."

End of doc — this is intentionally terse. If you need longer-form creative, generate a separate 'marketing copy pack' doc. For FastPass we keep it lean and operable.

(Last update: 2026-03-10 — staged for marketplace submission; track changes in linked PR)
